title: Pickleball & Golf Year 2026-27
conditions: Age 55. Right hip replacement (anterior approach, Mar 4, 2026), pain-free; mild arthritis in the left hip. Right calf tear (Sep 19, 2026), now pain-free, right calf still a bit weaker than the left. Right inner elbow (golfer's elbow pattern) flares with lots of pickleball plus golf. No shoulder pain; the shoulder work is for prevention.
disclaimer: Arnold is a coach, not a doctor. This is a training plan, not medical advice. If something feels wrong, stop and check with your doctor or physical therapist.
banner: Pain up to 3 out of 10 that settles by the next morning is OK. Higher, or worse the next morning: drop back a step. Calf swelling or warmth, a pop, night pain, or hip groin pain: stop and see your doctor or PT.

legs.name: Legs, hips and calves
legs.why: The hardest leg day. Best on a day that isn't the day before pickleball (for example Tuesday).

sport.name: Golf and pickleball: rotation, balance and footwork
sport.why: Moderate. Fine on Friday morning before golf, or on Saturday.

upper.name: Shoulders, back, arms and elbow
upper.why: Easy on the legs, so it's fine the day before pickleball (for example Sunday).

phases.name: Run-in
phases.ball: Ball 1 (lightest), waist to chest height, 20 circles each way building to 30
phases.goal: Learn the movements, wake up the tendons with gentle holds, and find comfortable weights. Low volume, nothing hard. Week 4 is Christmas week: lighter, plus a short retest so we have starting numbers.
phases.effort: Easy: leave 4 or more reps in the tank. Holds at about 5 to 6 out of 10 effort.

phases.name: Base: tendon and muscle building
phases.ball: Ball 2, then Ball 3 once Ball 2 is easy at shoulder height (usually around week 10)
phases.goal: Build tendon and muscle capacity (the general preparation phase): lots of isometric holds, slow 3-second lowering, moderate weights for 8 to 15 reps. Week 5 is New Year week and stays light. Week 9 is a recovery week, and week 13 is a recovery week that ends with a retest.
phases.effort: Leave 3 reps in the tank. Holds at about 6 to 7 out of 10 effort.

phases.name: Strength
phases.ball: Ball 3, then Ball 4 when Ball 3 is easy at shoulder height
phases.goal: Heavier, still slow and controlled: 5 to 8 reps, heavy slow calf raises, barbell Romanian deadlifts, slow pull-up lowering. Holds get heavier rather than longer. Week 17 is a recovery week, and week 21 is a recovery week with a retest.
phases.effort: Leave 2 reps in the tank. Holds at about 7 to 8 out of 10 effort.

phases.name: Power and sport-specific
phases.ball: Ball 4 (or stay on Ball 3 if 4 isn't easy yet)
phases.goal: Turn strength into quickness for pickleball and golf: lift fast and lower slowly with moderate weights, fast band rotations, footwork and braking, and small ankle hops only if you pass the hop checklist. Week 25 is a recovery week, and week 27 is a lighter week with a retest heading into summer.
phases.effort: Fast but crisp: end each set while every rep is still quick. Leave 3 reps in the tank on lifts.

phases.name: Peak and maintain (summer)
phases.ball: Ball 4, or Ball 3 in heavy-play weeks
phases.goal: Hold your strength and quickness while you play a lot of pickleball: fewer sets, the same weights, short sport drills, and plenty of elbow and calf care. Weeks 31 and 35 are recovery weeks. Week 39 (the end of August) is the final retest, and then the next year's cycle starts over.
phases.effort: Leave 2 to 3 reps in the tank. Short and sharp, never exhausting.

weeks.note: Christmas week (Dec 21 to 27): lighter on purpose.
New Year week (Dec 28 to Jan 3): lighter on purpose.

items.reps: 30 circles each way in each of the 4 positions, each arm
items.notes: Once a day at most: if you've already done it today, skip it here.
Then 1 or 2 slow lowerings if you feel good.

items.side: each arm, right first; right gets 1 extra set
items.notes: In heavy-play weeks, these holds are the only elbow work.

items.tempo: help it up with the other hand, then 4 seconds down
items.notes: Skip in heavy pickleball-plus-golf weeks.

warm_cardio.name: Easy cardio warm-up
warm_cardio.how: Pedal the upright bike or walk on the treadmill at an easy pace, enough to feel warm and breathe a little harder but still talk easily.
warm_cardio.swap: No bike or treadmill (The Villages): brisk walk outside, or march in place swinging your arms.

ankle_prep.name: Ankle circles and two-leg calf raises
ankle_prep.how: Draw 10 slow circles each way with each ankle, then do easy calf raises on both feet holding a counter.

leg_swings.name: Small leg swings, holding on
leg_swings.how: Hold a counter. Swing one leg gently forward and back, then side to side across your body, in a small, comfortable range. Never force the end of the swing.
leg_swings.easier: Make the swings smaller, or just march in place.

open_book.name: Side-lying open book (upper-back turn)
open_book.how: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked (a pillow between them is fine), arms straight in front. Lift the top arm up and over, turning your chest toward the ceiling and following your hand with your eyes. Breathe out as you open. This loosens the upper back for your golf turn without twisting your hips.
open_book.easier: Do it seated: arms crossed on your chest, turn your upper body gently side to side.

pullapart.name: Band pull-apart
pullapart.how: Hold a light band in front of your chest with straight arms. Pull it apart until it touches your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together and down. Return slowly.

shoulder_reliever.name: Shoulder Reliever circles (4 positions)
shoulder_reliever.how: Hold the Shoulder Reliever handle with the ball attached and your arm extended. Keep your wrist still and make the ball circle using your shoulder, not your wrist. Circle clockwise, then counterclockwise, in each of 4 positions: (1) arm straight out in front, (2) about halfway between front and side, (3) straight out to the side, (4) bent forward at the hips with your free hand on a wall or counter and the arm hanging a little away from your body (mind your shins). Then switch arms. If shoulder height pinches, do it at waist height and let it creep up over the weeks. The maker's rules: no more than once a day, and stay on each ball at least 10 days and until shoulder height feels easy in all 4 positions before moving to the next heavier ball (start the new ball back at waist height).
shoulder_reliever.easier: Lower the arm toward waist height, do fewer circles, or go back one ball.
shoulder_reliever.swap: Shoulder Reliever not with you: loop a light band around a door handle at chest height, hold the other end with a straight arm so the band is slightly tight, and draw small, quick circles from the shoulder in the same 4 positions (same counts). Or hold a light object, like a full water bottle, and do the same small circles. Maker's how-to page: https://shoulderreliever.com/pages/instructional-video

bridge.name: Glute bridge
bridge.how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. Squeeze your seat and lift your hips until your body is a straight line from knees to shoulders. Don't arch your lower back.
bridge.easier: Lift only halfway, or hold each rep at the top instead of doing more reps.

hip_thrust.name: Bench hip thrust with a dumbbell
hip_thrust.how: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long side of the bench and a dumbbell across your hips (hold it with both hands; a folded towel under it helps). Feet flat, knees bent. Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and body are level, squeeze, then lower under control.
hip_thrust.easier: Do floor glute bridges with the dumbbell on your hips instead.

box_squat.name: Box squat to the bench
box_squat.how: Stand in front of the bench (seat at knee height or higher) holding a dumbbell at your chest. Sit back slowly until you lightly touch the bench, pause without relaxing, then stand up. Knees follow your toes, weight in your heels, chest tall. Never go lower than the bench.
box_squat.easier: No weight, put a firm cushion on the bench so you don't go as low, or use your hands to help push up.

wall_sit.name: Shallow wall sit
wall_sit.how: Back flat on a wall, feet a step out. Slide down only until your knees are bent about a third of the way (nowhere near a chair position). Hold, weight in your heels, breathing normally.
wall_sit.easier: Slide down less, or shorten the hold.

db_hinge.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift (hip hinge)
db_hinge.how: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, knees soft. Push your hips back like closing a car door with your seat, sliding the weights down your thighs to just below your knees, back flat. Stand up by squeezing your seat. The hips go back; you don't squat down.
db_hinge.easier: Lighter dumbbells, or only go down to the top of your knees.

bb_rdl.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
bb_rdl.how: The same hip hinge, holding the barbell. To get the bar up safely, set it on two sturdy risers (for example the step and a stack of plates) so it starts about knee height, then stand up with it. From standing, push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs to just below the knees, back flat, then stand by squeezing your seat. Start with the bar plus light plates, and add 5 to 10 lb only when every set leaves 2 or more reps in the tank. No barbell squats, ever.
bb_rdl.easier: Use the dumbbell Romanian deadlift instead.

bb_top_hold.name: Barbell top hold (grip and posture)
bb_top_hold.how: Stand up with the barbell as for the Romanian deadlift and simply hold it at the top: tall, shoulders down, ribs down, squeezing the bar hard. Builds grip, forearm tendons and posture.
bb_top_hold.easier: Hold a pair of dumbbells instead (farmer hold).

step_up.name: Step-up onto the step
step_up.how: Put your whole foot on the step (6 to 8 inches), hand on a wall or rail. Push through that heel to stand up tall, then lower the other foot slowly back down. Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
step_up.easier: Use a lower step or more hand support.

step_down.name: Slow step-down
step_down.how: Stand on the step on one leg, holding a wall. Slowly bend that knee and lower the other heel toward the floor in front, tap lightly, then stand back up. Knee over your toes, hips level. This builds the braking strength you use when you stop at the kitchen line.
step_down.easier: Use a lower step, or only go halfway down.

split_hold.name: Short split-stance hold
split_hold.how: Stand in a short staggered stance (one foot a normal step ahead), holding a counter. Bend both knees only a few inches and hold, with your weight mostly on the front leg. No deep lunges.
split_hold.easier: Bend less, lean more on the counter, or shorten the hold.

sl_rdl.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift, hand on the wall
sl_rdl.how: Stand on one leg, fingertips on a wall or counter. Hinge forward at the hips as the free leg reaches straight back, hips level and back flat, only as far as is comfortable, then stand up tall. Great for balance, hips and golf posture.
sl_rdl.easier: Keep the back toe on the floor like a kickstand, and hinge less.

side_leg_lift.name: Side-lying leg lift
side_leg_lift.how: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent, top leg straight and slightly behind you, toes pointing forward. Lift the top leg about a foot, pause, lower slowly. Don't roll backward.
side_leg_lift.easier: Lift lower, or bend the top knee to shorten the lever.

clamshell.name: Clamshell with band
clamshell.how: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent, a band just above your knees. Keep your feet together and open the top knee like a clamshell, without rolling backward. Pause, close slowly.
clamshell.easier: No band, and a smaller opening.

wall_press_hold.name: Side hip wall press hold
wall_press_hold.how: Stand side-on to a wall, about a hand's width away. Lift the knee nearest the wall to hip height (or lower) and press the outside of that knee into the wall while standing tall on the other leg. Both hips work hard. Hold, then switch sides.
wall_press_hold.easier: Lift the knee less, press more gently, or hold a counter with the other hand.

band_walk.name: Side-step band walk
band_walk.how: Band just above your knees. Knees slightly bent, chest tall. Step sideways with control, keeping tension on the band, toes pointing forward.

adductor_squeeze.name: Inner-thigh squeeze hold
adductor_squeeze.how: Lie on your back, knees bent, a firm pillow or rolled towel between your knees. Squeeze and hold, breathing normally. Builds the inner-thigh strength you need for side-to-side pickleball moves.

adductor_side_plank.name: Inner-thigh side plank, knee on the bench
adductor_side_plank.how: Lie on your side next to the bench, propped on your elbow, with the inside of your top knee resting on the bench and the bottom leg hanging. Lift your hips so your body is straight and hold. Short-lever version only.
adductor_side_plank.easier: Do the inner-thigh squeeze hold instead.

calf_hold.name: Calf raise hold
calf_hold.how: Hold a counter. Rise onto the balls of your feet to about halfway up and hold there, steady, without bouncing. Single-leg when the workout says so (lift the other foot behind you). The right calf is still a bit weaker, so it gets the extra set. When the workout lists a dumbbell, hold it in the same-side hand.
calf_hold.easier: Two legs instead of one, a lower height, or less time.

calf_slow.name: Slow calf raise, straight knee
calf_slow.how: Hold a counter. Rise as high as you can over 3 seconds, hold a moment, and lower over 3 seconds. When the workout says 'step edge', stand on the edge of the step so your heel can drop a little below it at the bottom. Add a dumbbell in the same-side hand as you get stronger. This heavy, slow calf work rebuilds the tendon.
calf_slow.easier: Do it on the flat floor, or on two legs.

calf_bent.name: Bent-knee calf raise (seated with dumbbells)
calf_bent.how: Sit on the bench with the balls of your feet on a plate or the step and dumbbells resting on your knees (hands holding them steady). Lift your heels as high as you can, hold a moment, and lower slowly. This works the lower calf muscle (the soleus), which matters a lot for pickleball footwork.
calf_bent.easier: Lighter dumbbells, or no step under your feet.

quick_feet.name: Quick feet in place
quick_feet.how: Ready position (knees soft, weight on the balls of your feet). Take fast, tiny steps in place with your feet barely leaving the floor. Light and quiet.

pogo.name: Small two-foot ankle hops
pogo.how: Only once you pass the hop checklist in the notes. On both feet, in shoes, on a forgiving surface: small quick hops from the ankles, 1 to 2 inches off the floor, knees nearly straight, landing quietly. Stop at the first sign of calf or hip pain.
pogo.easier: Quick feet in place instead (no hopping).

line_hops.name: Small side-to-side line hops
line_hops.how: Only once you pass the hop checklist. Feet together, hop a few inches side to side over a line, landing softly and quietly. Small and quick, not high.
line_hops.easier: Quick side-steps over the line instead (no hop).

incline_pushup.name: Incline push-up on the bench or counter
incline_pushup.how: Hands on the edge of the bench or a counter, body in a straight line. Lower your chest toward it, elbows angled back about 45 degrees, then push away. The higher your hands, the easier it is.
incline_pushup.easier: Use a higher surface (counter or wall).

pushup_plus.name: Incline push-up plus
pushup_plus.how: Do an incline push-up, and at the top push a little further so your shoulder blades spread around your ribs (your upper back rounds slightly). That last bit works the muscle that keeps the shoulder blade snug on the ribs.

incline_press.name: Incline bench dumbbell press
incline_press.how: Set the bench to a low incline. Lie back with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, elbows angled back about 45 degrees. Press up until your arms are straight, then lower slowly.

db_row.name: Bench-supported one-arm row
db_row.how: One hand on the bench with both feet on the floor (kinder to the hips than kneeling on the bench), back flat. Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, squeezing the shoulder blade back and down, then lower slowly.
db_row.easier: Lighter dumbbell, or a band row anchored in a door.

face_pull.name: Band face pull
face_pull.how: Anchor a band at head height. Hold both ends, thumbs pointing back. Pull toward your face with elbows high and wide, finishing with your hands beside your ears as if showing off your biceps. Return slowly.

er_side.name: Band outward rotation, elbow at your side
er_side.how: Band anchored at elbow height to your side. Elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked against your side (a rolled towel under the arm helps). Rotate your forearm outward, away from your belly, keeping the elbow in place, then return slowly.

er_hold.name: Outward rotation hold in a doorway
er_hold.how: Stand in a doorway with your elbow bent 90 degrees at your side and the back of your wrist against the door frame. Press outward into the frame (nothing moves) and hold.

er_goalpost.name: Band outward rotation, arm out to the side
er_goalpost.how: Band anchored in front of you at shoulder height. Raise your upper arm out to the side to shoulder height with the elbow bent 90 degrees and the forearm pointing forward (like a goalpost). Rotate the forearm up until it points to the ceiling, then lower slowly. This is the position you serve and hit overheads from.
er_goalpost.easier: Keep the elbow a bit below shoulder height, or use the elbow-at-your-side version.

y_raise.name: Incline bench Y raise
y_raise.how: Set the bench to a medium incline and lie face down on it, arms hanging, thumbs up. Raise your arms up and out in a Y to about ear level, squeezing your shoulder blades down, then lower slowly. Start with no weight; use the 10 lb dumbbells only when it's easy.
y_raise.easier: Raise to a T (straight out to the sides) instead, or stand and use a light band.

overhead_hold.name: Overhead dumbbell hold
overhead_hold.how: Press one dumbbell overhead and hold it there with a straight arm, biceps near your ear, ribs down, standing tall (walk slowly if you like). Builds overhead shoulder tolerance.
overhead_hold.easier: Hold the dumbbell at shoulder height instead, or use a light band overhead.

db_press.name: Standing one-arm dumbbell press
db_press.how: Stand tall, a dumbbell at your shoulder, palm facing in. Press straight up without leaning back, then lower slowly.
db_press.easier: Sit on the bench with the back upright, or go lighter.

wall_slide.name: Wall slide with band
wall_slide.how: Face a wall with your forearms on it and a light band around your wrists. Push gently outward into the band and slide your forearms up the wall as high as is comfortable, then back down.
wall_slide.easier: No band, and only partway up.

dead_hang.name: Dead hang with feet helping
dead_hang.how: Grip the pull-up bar shoulder-width. Keep your feet on a step or the floor taking some of your weight, and let your body hang with your shoulders gently engaged (not shrugged to your ears). Take a little more weight off your feet over the weeks.
dead_hang.easier: More weight on your feet, or shorter holds.
dead_hang.swap: No pull-up bar (The Villages): band pulldown hold. Anchor a band high in a door. Kneel or sit, pull your elbows down to your sides so your hands are at shoulder level, squeeze your shoulder blades down, and hold.

scap_hang.name: Shoulder-blade pull on the bar
scap_hang.how: Hang from the bar (feet helping if needed). Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and back so your body rises an inch, hold 3 seconds, then relax back to the hang.
scap_hang.easier: Keep more weight on your feet.
scap_hang.swap: No pull-up bar (The Villages): band pulldown hold. Anchor a band high in a door. Kneel or sit, pull your elbows down to your sides so your hands are at shoulder level, squeeze your shoulder blades down, and hold.

top_hold.name: Top-of-pull-up hold
top_hold.how: Use a step or chair to get your chin over the bar (or as high as you can), then take your feet away and hold, elbows bent, chest up. Step back down; don't drop.
top_hold.easier: Hold with the elbows bent halfway, or keep a toe on the step.
top_hold.swap: No pull-up bar (The Villages): band pulldown hold. Anchor a band high in a door. Kneel or sit, pull your elbows down to your sides so your hands are at shoulder level, squeeze your shoulder blades down, and hold.

slow_lower.name: Slow pull-up lowering
slow_lower.how: Step up so your chin is over the bar, take your feet away, then lower yourself as slowly as you can (aim for 4 to 5 seconds) to a straight-arm hang. Step back up and repeat. The quickest route from 1 pull-up to several.
slow_lower.easier: Top-of-pull-up hold instead, or lower with a toe on the chair.
slow_lower.swap: No pull-up bar: slow band pulldown. Anchor the band high, pull your elbows down to your sides, then let the band pull your arms back up over 4 seconds.

wrist_flex_hold.name: Palm-up wrist hold (inner elbow tendon)
wrist_flex_hold.how: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or the bench, palm up, hand just past the edge, holding a dumbbell. Keep the wrist level and still. This loads the inner-elbow tendon gently and often eases golfer's elbow pain. The right arm gets the extra set.
wrist_flex_hold.easier: Press your palm up into the underside of a table instead of holding a dumbbell, or press gently.

pronation_hold.name: Forearm turn-in hold
pronation_hold.how: Sit with your forearm on your thigh, elbow bent, holding a dumbbell by one end only, like a hammer, standing upright. Let the palm turn slightly toward the floor so the weight leans inward, and hold it there without moving. Choke up on the handle to make it easier.
pronation_hold.easier: Hold closer to the weighted end, or press your hand against your other hand.

wrist_flex_lower.name: Slow palm-up wrist lowering
wrist_flex_lower.how: Forearm on your thigh or the bench, palm up, dumbbell in hand. Use your other hand to help lift the weight up (wrist curled), then let go and lower it slowly with just the working hand over 4 seconds. Help it back up and repeat. This slow-lowering type of loading is what helped golfer's elbow in the research. If you get a rubber FlexBar (about $20), the Reverse Tyler Twist can replace this: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LtR8fYEUnXI
wrist_flex_lower.easier: Lighter dumbbell or a shorter range.

pronation_lower.name: Slow forearm turn-in lowering
pronation_lower.how: Hold the dumbbell by one end like a hammer, forearm on your thigh. Use the other hand to help turn the palm up, then let go and slowly let the palm turn back down toward the floor over 3 to 4 seconds, resisting with your forearm. Help it back and repeat.
pronation_lower.easier: Hold the handle closer to the weighted end.

farmer_hold.name: Farmer hold
farmer_hold.how: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Stand tall, shoulders down and back, and squeeze the handles. Walk slowly if you like.

suitcase_hold.name: One-arm suitcase hold
suitcase_hold.how: Hold one heavy dumbbell at your side like a suitcase and stand perfectly straight, not leaning. Walk slowly if you like. Works grip and the side core muscles that stop you tipping.

dead_bug.name: Dead bug
dead_bug.how: Lie on your back, arms up, knees bent over your hips. Press your lower back gently into the floor. Slowly reach one arm overhead and straighten the opposite leg toward the floor, then return and switch. Keep your back flat.
dead_bug.easier: Move only the arms, or tap a heel to the floor with the knee bent.

side_plank.name: Side plank
side_plank.how: Lie on your side propped on your elbow, elbow under your shoulder. Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to knees (knees bent) or, later, head to feet. Hold.
side_plank.easier: Knees bent, or lean on the bench at an angle.

pallof_hold.name: Band anti-rotation hold (Pallof hold)
pallof_hold.how: Anchor a band at chest height to your side. Stand side-on, feet hip-width, holding the band at your chest with both hands. Press your hands straight out and hold, not letting the band turn you. This trains your core to resist twisting, which protects your back in golf and pickleball.
pallof_hold.easier: Step closer to the anchor for less tension.

pallof_press.name: Band anti-rotation press (Pallof press)
pallof_press.how: Same setup as the hold. Press the band out, hold, bring it back, staying square the whole time.

band_chop.name: Band chop, high to low
band_chop.how: Band anchored high to one side. Hold it with both hands and pull it down and across your body to the opposite hip, turning your chest and letting your back heel pivot so your hips turn together with your shoulders (no twisting at the hip joint). Return slowly. Smooth, not jerky.

band_lift.name: Band lift, low to high
band_lift.how: Band anchored low to one side. Pull it up and across your body to the opposite shoulder, turning your chest and pivoting your back foot, then return slowly. Like a forehand drive.

fast_chop.name: Fast band chop or lift
fast_chop.how: Same as the band chop or lift, but pull quickly and smoothly, then return slowly over 3 seconds. Stay balanced, feet pivoting together. Builds swing speed safely.

golf_turn.name: Golf-posture turn with a club
golf_turn.how: Hold a club across your chest and take your golf posture. Turn your upper body back and through slowly, letting your hips turn naturally with you. Then make a few slow practice swings, pausing at the top for 2 seconds.

sl_balance.name: Single-leg balance
sl_balance.how: Stand on one leg next to a counter, knee soft. The workout tells you which version: eyes open, slow head turns, tossing a ball hand to hand, or eyes closed (only with a counter right there).
sl_balance.easier: Lightly touch the counter or the other toe down.

side_stick.name: Side step and stick
side_stick.how: From a ready position, take one big step to the side, land softly with the knee bent over your toes, and hold still for 2 seconds. Step back and repeat. Teaches braking when you reach for a wide ball.
side_stick.easier: Smaller steps, hand near a counter.

shuffle_stop.name: Shuffle and stop
shuffle_stop.how: Shuffle 2 or 3 steps sideways, then stop firmly on the outside leg and hold for 2 seconds. Go back the other way. Quick feet, quiet stops.
shuffle_stop.easier: Walk the steps instead of shuffling.

split_step.name: Pickleball split step and react
split_step.how: Walk forward 2 steps, do a small split step (a tiny bounce onto both feet into a ready position), then step out left or right as if moving to a ball. Small and light. Until you pass the hop checklist, keep the bounce on the ground (heels lift, toes stay down).
split_step.easier: No bounce: stop in a ready position and step out.

brake_step.name: Forward step and brake
brake_step.how: Walk 2 or 3 quick steps forward, then stop within 2 steps in a balanced ready position, knees bent and chest up, like arriving at the kitchen line. Hold 2 seconds.

bike_intervals.name: Optional bike intervals
bike_intervals.how: Fayetteville. Assault bike or upright bike: 20 seconds of hard pedaling, then 40 seconds easy. Hard means you couldn't hold a conversation, not an all-out sprint.
bike_intervals.swap: The Villages: a brisk walk with 20 seconds of fast walking every minute, or 20 seconds of quick feet.

calf_stretch.name: Wall calf stretch, straight then bent knee
calf_stretch.how: Hands on a wall, one foot back, heel down. Lean in with the back knee straight, then bend the back knee slightly and lean again (that reaches the lower calf).

hip_front_stretch.name: Gentle standing hip-front stretch
hip_front_stretch.how: Stand in a short staggered stance holding a counter. Tuck your seat under and shift forward gently until you feel a mild stretch in the front of the back hip. Mild only: no forcing, no lunging.

forearm_stretch.name: Forearm stretch, palm up
forearm_stretch.how: Arm straight in front, palm up. With the other hand, gently pull the fingers down and back until you feel a mild stretch in the inner forearm.

doorway_stretch.name: Doorway chest stretch
doorway_stretch.how: Forearm on a door frame, elbow at shoulder height. Step through gently until you feel a stretch across the front of the chest and shoulder.

test_calf.name: Test: calf raise count, each leg
test_calf.how: Single leg, fingertips on a wall, flat floor. Count full-height raises at a steady pace (about 2 seconds up, 2 down) until you can't reach full height or your form breaks. Record both, for example 'R 22, L 27'. Goal: right within 90 percent of left, and 25 or more each side.

test_chair.name: Test: 30-second sit-to-stand
test_chair.how: Bench at knee height, arms crossed on your chest. Count how many times you stand up fully and sit back down in 30 seconds. A standard test for adults 50 and up.
test_chair.easier: Use your hands, and note that you did.

test_balance.name: Test: single-leg balance
test_balance.how: Each leg, next to a counter: time how long you can stand on one leg with eyes open (stop at 60 seconds), then eyes closed (stop at 20 seconds).

test_side_plank.name: Test: side plank hold
test_side_plank.how: Side plank on whichever version you've been training (knees or feet). Time each side, up to 60 seconds, stopping when your hips sag.

test_grip.name: Test: farmer hold time
test_grip.how: Two 30 lb dumbbells (two 50s from the strength phase on). Time how long you can hold them standing tall, up to 90 seconds. Note which weight you used.

test_hang.name: Test: hang or pulldown hold
test_hang.how: Fayetteville: time a full dead hang (feet off) up to 60 seconds, and count strict pull-ups if you like. The Villages: time the band pulldown hold up to 60 seconds. Record which one you did.

test_elbow.name: Test: elbow and shoulder check
test_elbow.how: Palm-up wrist hold with 15 lb for 30 seconds, right arm: record inner-elbow pain 0 to 10. Then 10 band outward rotations with the arm out to the side: record shoulder pain 0 to 10. Both should be 0 to 2.

notes: Workouts are a numbered list, not dates. Do the next one whenever you can; aim for about 3 a week (for example Sunday, Tuesday, and Friday or Saturday). Days off don't matter.

Each week runs Legs, then Sport, then Upper. On a Sunday-Tuesday-Friday rhythm that puts the hard leg day on Tuesday (two days before Thursday pickleball), the sport day on Friday or Saturday, and the easy-on-the-legs upper day on Sunday, the day before Monday pickleball.
If the next workout is a Legs day and you play pickleball tomorrow, it's fine to do the following workout first. The app keeps the skipped one as your next workout until you do it.

Pain rule: joint or tendon pain up to 3 out of 10 during exercise is OK if it settles by the next morning. If it goes above 3, or you're worse the next morning, drop back a step: use the previous week's weight or hold, or the easier option.

Going up: when every set feels easy (3 or more reps left in the tank, or holds feel like 5 out of 10 or less) for 2 workouts in a row and pain stays at 0 to 2, move up one dumbbell (10, 15, 20, 30, 50 lb), add 5 to 10 lb on the barbell, or add 5 to 10 seconds to a hold. The weights listed are a guide; your log wins.
Big jumps between dumbbells (30 to 50 lb): bridge the gap with slower lowering, an extra rep or two, or a backpack with books.
Missed time: after 7 to 14 days off, repeat the last workout you did before moving on (open it and mark it done again, or just redo it). After 3 or more weeks off, go back about 3 workouts.
Recovery weeks are lighter on purpose (about 40 percent fewer sets). Do them even if you feel great; that's when the tendons catch up.

Retests come at the end of each phase in the Sport workout: calf raise count each leg, 30-second sit-to-stand, single-leg balance, side plank, farmer hold time, hang or pulldown hold, and an elbow and shoulder check.

Elbow rule for heavy weeks: in any week with 3 or more pickleball days plus golf, back-to-back days of both, or inner-elbow pain above 3 out of 10 (or still there the next morning), skip the slow wrist lowering, the farmer hold, the barbell top hold and the bar hangs, and keep only the gentle palm-up wrist holds (they tend to calm tendon pain). Go back to normal the next week if the elbow is at 0 to 2. Also check your paddle and club grip size, and don't strangle the grip.

Hop checklist (before any ankle hops, line hops or a split-step bounce off the ground): 25 or more single-leg calf raises on the right, within about 90 percent of the left; no calf pain during or the next morning for 2 weeks; hips quiet (no groin pain or painful clicking). If anything is missing, use the no-hop option listed.

Hips: no deep loaded squats or lunges, no barbell squats, no hard jumping, no heavy loaded twisting at the hip. Rotation exercises turn the upper body with the hips and back foot pivoting together. Every lower-body exercise lists an easier option.

Shoulder Reliever: it's in the Sport and Upper workouts (about twice a week). The maker says no more than once a day. Stay on each ball at least 10 days and until all 4 positions at shoulder height feel easy, then start the next ball back at waist height. Not with you? Each workout lists a band swap.

Optional items: the pull-up bar and bike work are Fayetteville only; each lists a swap for The Villages. Everything else uses dumbbells, bands, the barbell, the bench, the step and the curl bar, which you have at both houses.
Effort in plain English: 'leave 3 reps in the tank' means stop when you could still do about 3 more good reps. Hold effort is out of 10, where 10 is the hardest you could push.
redFlags: Calf swelling, warmth or redness, or new deep calf pain (can be a blood clot: get checked the same day)
A pop or sudden sharp pain in the calf, elbow or shoulder
Pain at night or at rest that is new or getting worse
Hip groin pain, clicking with pain, a feeling of the hip giving way, or a sudden change in how the hip moves
Numbness or tingling down the arm, or the elbow or shoulder getting weaker
Chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness or fainting
